title: Zombies vs Plants — Card Research

groups.label: Plants
groups.description: Broad Plant research for the shared pool. Overgrowth is confirmed green for the first Jumpstart box, with early plays to support its partners.

groups.label: Treefolk
groups.description: Ancient Grove is confirmed white: stompy Treefolk, nature spirits, and actual bird allies. Preferred early birds are Healer's Hawk, Rustwing Falcon, and Suntail Hawk, preserving singleton variety. Test the combined curve with each Plant partner; retain other colors for the cube.

groups.label: Fungi
groups.description: Spore Swarm is confirmed black: early Fungi, death value, and token support that work without green mana. Retain other colors and more elaborate engines for the shared cube research.

groups.label: Botanical allies
groups.description: Botanical Elementals and other discoveries to investigate across the shortlist. Group tags describe themes; explicit faction alignment takes precedence.

groups.label: Living lands
groups.description: Animated forests and swamps and their support. Wild Awakening is confirmed green, with simple land-animation effects and early plays; complex and off-color discoveries remain for the cube.

groups.label: Black · Necromancy
groups.description: Black necromancy, sacrifice, and recurring Zombies for the proposed Restless Dead packet.

groups.label: Blue · Stitched creations
groups.description: Blue stitched Zombies, graveyard setup, and strange experiments for the proposed Stitched Together packet.

groups.label: White · Mummies
groups.description: White mummies, coordinated creatures, embalming, and protection for the proposed Tomb Guard packet.

groups.label: Green · The Turned
groups.description: The Turned targets simple green-paid Zombies, prioritizing turned plant life where practical. Black-green and three-color candidates remain visible as shared research for the cube.

groups.label: Mana support
groups.description: Flexible lands and fixing for combined Jumpstart decks and the wider multicolor cube research.

retentionPolicy: Retain every candidate and its source notes for Jumpstart rebalancing and a future cube, including cards omitted from any draft. Versioned packet selections and replacement reasons must not delete unused research.

research.note: Lets high-toughness Plants, Treefolk, and Fungi deal useful combat damage without requiring shared creature types.

cards.name: Anointed Procession

research.caution: Does not make a token by itself. It doubles other tokens too, but that generic utility is not a claim that it is specifically botanical. Can become very strong with repeated production.
research.manaNote: Costs 3W.

cards.name: Armored Skaab

cards.name: Beza, the Bounding Spring
cards.oracle_text: When Beza enters, create a Treasure token if an opponent controls more lands than you. You gain 4 life if an opponent has more life than you. Create two 1/1 blue Fish creature tokens if an opponent controls more creatures than you. Draw a card if an opponent has more cards in hand than you.

rulings.comment: You compare the number of lands you control with the number of lands each opponent controls as Beza's ability resolves. At that time, if at least one opponent controls more lands than you, you'll create a Treasure token. Similarly, you compare life totals, creatures controlled, and cards in hand with each opponent as Beza's ability resolves. If at least one opponent has more life, creatures, or cards in hand than you, you'll get the appropriate bonus. It doesn't matter if you qualified for any of the previous bonuses or not.
In a multiplayer game, you consider each opponent. If you have fewer lands than one opponent and less life than another, for example, you'll get both of those bonuses.

No player may take any actions while Beza's ability is resolving. For example, you can't use the Treasure token to try and change the outcome of any of the other comparisons. However, in some unusual cases, that Treasure token might enter as a creature, in which case it might impact whether you get Fish or not.

research.note: User-nominated Elemental Elk for the white botanical theme. A 4/5 body can supply the combined deck's larger threats, with independent catch-up bonuses on entry.
research.caution: Checks lands, life, creature count, and hand size separately. Treasure and blue Fish tokens add components and rules text; review power and simplicity before selecting.
research.manaNote: Four mana including WW. No off-color mana is needed for its Fish or Treasure tokens.

cards.oracle_text: {4}, {T}: Create a 2/2 colorless Shapeshifter creature token with changeling. (It is every creature type.)

research.caution: Creates Shapeshifters with changeling rather than dedicated botanical tokens. They are mechanically every creature type, but that should not replace a deliberate thematic choice; the repeated four-mana activation is slow.

research.manaNote: Four mana with one green pip is easy to share with a second color.

cards.oracle_text:

research.manaNote: Two mana with one green pip.

cards.name: Blossoming Defense
cards.oracle_text: Target creature you control gets +2/+2 and gains hexproof until end of turn. (It can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control.)

research.caution: Hexproof does not stop untargeted destruction or combat damage; the effect lasts only for the turn.
research.manaNote: Single green mana.

cards.name: Bosk Banneret

research.note: Supports an otherwise expensive Treefolk curve and also discounts partner creatures that happen to be Shamans.

cards.oracle_text:
Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, put a +1/+1 counter on target creature.
{3}{G}{G}: Double the number of +1/+1 counters on each creature you control.

cards.name: Cactusfolk Sureshot
cards.oracle_text:
Reach
Ward {2} (Whenever this creature becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, counter it unless that player pays {2}.)
At the beginning of combat on your turn, other creatures you control with power 4 or greater gain trample and haste until end of turn.

research.note: Gives sufficiently large Plants or Treefolk haste and trample while remaining a substantial attacker itself.
research.caution: Its combat trigger checks power four or greater and does not help small Saprolings without other growth.
research.manaNote: Requires both red and green; include reliable access within its own packet.

cards.name: Call of the Death-Dweller
cards.oracle_text: Return up to two target creature cards with total mana value 3 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield. Put a deathtouch counter on either of them. Then put a menace counter on either of them.

research.note: Can recover two small creatures from either packet and enhance them with keyword counters.
research.caution: Returned creatures must total mana value three or less; deathtouch and menace counters require tracking.

cards.name: Candlegrove Witch
cards.oracle_text: Coven — At the beginning of combat on your turn, if you control three or more creatures with different powers, this creature gains flying until end of turn.
cards.flavor_text: "Like a thousand candles fighting back the darkness, we are strongest when we stand together."

rulings.comment: For three creatures to have different powers from one another, each of their powers needs to be different. A 1/1 creature, a 2/1 creature, and another 2/1 creature aren't three creatures with different powers, even though both 2/1 creatures have different power than the 1/1 creature.
A creature has different power from another if their powers are different numbers. For example, a 1/1 creature and a 2/1 creature have different powers.

Many coven abilities, such as that of Dawnhart Wardens above, are triggered abilities with intervening if clauses. You must control three or more creatures with different powers at the time the ability triggers and at the time the ability tries to resolve. They do not, however, need to be the same set of creatures in both cases.

research.note: A forest-art search lead and grove-practitioner candidate. Its two-mana 2/2 body works with every partner. Different-sized Treefolk, Fungi, and tokens may enable its optional flying payoff.
research.caution: Coven checks for three or more creatures with different powers when the beginning-of-combat ability would trigger and when it resolves. Adds a board-counting condition; the Warlock type alone does not establish botanical identity.
research.manaNote: Costs 1W; no partner color or additional mana payment needed for coven.

cards.name: Cast Out

cards.name: Observant Alseid
cards.oracle_text:
Bestow {4}{W} (If you cast this card for its bestow cost, it's an Aura spell with enchant creature. It becomes a creature again if it's not attached.)
Vigilance
Enchanted creature gets +2/+2 and has vigilance.

rulings.comment: On the stack, a spell with bestow is either a creature spell or an Aura spell. It's never both, although it's an enchantment spell in either case.

Unlike other Aura spells, an Aura spell with bestow isn't countered if its target is illegal as it begins to resolve. Rather, the effect making it an Aura spell ends, it loses enchant creature, it returns to being an enchantment creature spell, and it resolves and enters the battlefield as an enchantment creature.

Unlike other Auras, an Aura with bestow isn't put into its owner's graveyard if it becomes unattached. Rather, the effect making it an Aura ends, it loses enchant creature, and it remains on the battlefield as an enchantment creature. It can attack (and its {T} abilities can be activated, if it has any) on the turn it becomes unattached if it's been under your control continuously, even as an Aura, since your most recent turn began.
If a permanent with bestow enters the battlefield by any method other than being cast, it will be an enchantment creature. You can't choose to pay the bestow cost and have it become an Aura.
Auras attached to a creature don't become tapped when the creature becomes tapped. Except in some rare cases, an Aura with bestow remains untapped when it becomes unattached and becomes a creature.

research.note: An owner-nominated Nymph that can be played as a three-mana 2/2 with vigilance or later bestowed to strengthen a creature from either packet. It does not require other enchantments to function.
research.caution: Neither the three-mana body nor five-mana bestow improves the one- and two-drop gap. Bestow's creature/Aura transitions add rules load, so retain as a lower-priority or cube candidate.
research.manaNote: Creature cost 2W; optional bestow cost 4W.

cards.name: Scion of Vitu-Ghazi
cards.oracle_text: When this creature enters, if you cast it from your hand, create a 1/1 white Bird creature token with flying, then populate. (Create a token that's a copy of a creature token you control.)

rulings.comment: The new creature token copies the characteristics of the original token as stated by the effect that created the original token.

Populate doesn't target the creature token you're copying. You choose that creature token as you're taking the populate action. You can choose any creature token you control. If a spell or ability causes you to create a creature token and then instructs you to populate, you may choose to copy the token you just created, or you may choose to copy another creature token you control.
If you choose to copy a creature token that's a copy of another creature, the new creature token will copy the characteristics of whatever the original token is copying.
If you control no creature tokens when you populate, nothing will happen.

The new token doesn't copy whether the original token is tapped or untapped, whether it has any counters on it or Auras and Equipment attached to it, or any noncopy effects that have changed its power, toughness, color, and so on.

Any enters-the-battlefield abilities of the copied token will trigger when the new token enters the battlefield. Any "as [this creature] enters the battlefield" or "[this creature] enters the battlefield with" abilities of the copied token will also work.
If a creature (such as Clone) enters the battlefield as a copy of this creature, the copy's "enters-the-battlefield" ability will still trigger as long as you cast that creature spell from your hand.

research.note: User-nominated botanical Elemental for white Treefolk support. When cast from hand it creates a Bird before populating, so it supplies its own token; it can instead copy a suitable creature token from the other packet.
research.caution: Five mana does not improve the early curve. The token ability requires casting from hand and populate adds a token-copy decision.
research.manaNote: Five mana including WW.

cards.name: Skullbriar, the Walking Grave
cards.oracle_text:
Haste
Whenever Skullbriar deals combat damage to a player, put a +1/+1 counter on it.
Counters remain on Skullbriar as it moves to any zone other than a player's hand or library.

rulings.comment: Skullbriar will get one +1/+1 counter each time it deals combat damage to a player (including you if its combat damage gets redirected), regardless of how much damage is dealt.
Skullbriar retains all counters, not just +1/+1 counters.
The counters that remain on Skullbriar as it changes zones aren't "placed" on Skullbriar. Effects like Doubling Season's and Melira, Sylvok Outcast's won't affect those counters.

Counters that adjust power and/or toughness affect Skullbriar's power and/or toughness in zones other than the battlefield. For example, a Skullbriar in the command zone with a +1/+1 counter on it will be 2/2.

Effects that last "for as long as that creature has a [kind of] counter on it," such as Aven Mimeomancer's, stop applying to Skullbriar once it leaves the battlefield. Even though Skullbriar retains the counters, it becomes a new object with no relation to its last existence in its previous zone.

Skullbriar's last ability only works if it has that ability in the zone it's moving from. For example, with Yixlid Jailer ("Cards in graveyards lose all abilities") on the battlefield, a Skullbriar with a counter on it in a graveyard loses that counter when it's put onto the battlefield. Conversely, that Skullbriar moving from the graveyard to the battlefield would retain that counter if Humility ("All creatures lose all abilities and are 1/1") were on the battlefield; if Skullbriar then left the battlefield with Humility still on the battlefield, it would lose the counter.

If a card becomes a copy of Skullbriar, counters will remain on that card when it leaves the battlefield (unless it goes to your hand or library). Once it does so, it stops being a copy of Skullbriar, so those counters will cease to exist when that card next changes zones.

research.note: A plant-like mass of roots and overgrowth animated as a Zombie Elemental: a priority botanical undead candidate assigned exclusively to the Zombie faction even though its type line does not say Plant. Haste and combat damage grow it, while retained counters reward returning it from the graveyard.
research.caution: Retains every kind of counter, including harmful counters, when changing zones except to a hand or library. This unusual exception adds tracking complexity; it is neither a Plant nor a Treefolk for type-specific bonuses.
research.manaNote: Costs BG, needing both black and green early. A thematic fit with black Zombies does not make it castable in an otherwise black-white or black-blue pairing without fixing.

research.caution: Triggers on every upkeep, not only yours. The body is an Elemental and the tokens are Saprolings; neither is automatically a Plant or Fungus. Its continuing production may overwhelm a low-power game.
research.manaNote: Costs 5GGG, so both total cost and triple-green requirements are significant.

cards.name: Verdeloth the Ancient
cards.oracle_text:
Kicker {X} (You may pay an additional {X} as you cast this spell.)
Saproling creatures and other Treefolk creatures get +1/+1.
When Verdeloth enters, if it was kicked, create X 1/1 green Saproling creature tokens.

research.note: A direct bridge between Treefolk and Saproling-producing Fungus cards, with optional token production on entry.
research.caution: Its Saproling and Treefolk bonuses are global, not limited to its controller; ordinary Plants do not qualify.
research.manaNote: Six mana with double green before any optional generic kicker payment.

cards.name: Victimize
cards.oracle_text: Choose two target creature cards in your graveyard. Sacrifice a creature. If you do, return the chosen cards to the battlefield tapped.

research.note: Can trade an expendable creature for two creatures from your graveyard, recycling partner-color bodies and entry effects.
research.caution: Requires two creature-card targets before resolution, then a creature to sacrifice. The returned creatures enter tapped; the sacrificed creature cannot be one of the initially chosen targets.
research.manaNote: Costs 2B.

cards.name: Vigean Hydropon
cards.oracle_text:
Graft 5 (This creature enters with five +1/+1 counters on it. Whenever another creature enters, you may move a +1/+1 counter from this creature onto it.)
This creature can't attack or block.

research.note: Distributes counters to incoming Treefolk, Plants, or Fungus creatures and works with counter multipliers.
research.caution: Cannot attack or block at all; requires later creatures and creates a substantial tempo cost.
research.manaNote: Requires green and blue at three mana.

cards.name: Vinelasher Kudzu
cards.oracle_text: Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature.

research.note: A straightforward threat that grows from normal land drops and appreciates either partner's land search.
research.caution: A late draw may remain small without extra land drops.
research.manaNote: Two mana with one green pip.

cards.name: Vines of Vastwood
cards.oracle_text:
Kicker {G} (You may pay an additional {G} as you cast this spell.)
Target creature can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control this turn. If this spell was kicked, that creature gets +4/+4 until end of turn.

research.note: Vines protect a chosen creature from opposing targeting, with an optional substantial combat boost for any faction creature.
research.caution: Its targeting restriction is not the hexproof keyword and can target opposing creatures; explain that distinction when relevant.
research.manaNote: One green normally; a second green pays the kicker for the boost.

cards.name: Vitu-Ghazi, the City-Tree
cards.oracle_text:
{T}: Add {C}.
{2}{G}{W}, {T}: Create a 1/1 green Saproling creature token.

research.note: Adds a repeatable Saproling source to the mana base for games that reach spare-mana turns.
research.caution: Normally produces only colorless mana; token creation consumes its tap plus four other mana, slowing color access if overused.
research.manaNote: Produces colorless, while token production requires 2GW and tapping this land.

cards.name: Vivisection
cards.oracle_text:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice a creature.
Draw three cards.

research.note: A grisly laboratory experiment that turns an expendable creature into three cards, fitting the stitched-creature theme and black death payoffs.
research.caution: Sacrificing a creature is an additional casting cost, so the creature is lost even if the spell is countered.
research.manaNote: Costs 3U plus sacrificing a creature.

cards.name: Vulturous Zombie
cards.oracle_text:
Flying
Whenever a card is put into an opponent's graveyard from anywhere, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature.

research.note: A flying Plant Zombie that grows when cards enter an opponent's graveyard, giving the crossover pool an aerial threat.
research.caution: Triggers on an opponent's graveyard, not its controller's. A growing flyer may be particularly strong against ground-focused Plants.
research.manaNote: Requires both black and green.

research.note: Selected for v0.1 Restless Dead: Simple two-mana Zombie body..
research.caution: Provisional selection; evaluate in the combined forty-card pairings.

cards.name: Wall of Blossoms
cards.oracle_text:
Defender
When this creature enters, draw a card.

research.note: Replaces itself while holding the ground, helping a slow Treefolk partner or a sacrifice-oriented Fungus partner.
research.caution: Defender keeps it from contributing to ordinary attacks.
research.manaNote: Two mana with one green pip.

cards.name: Wall of Kelp
cards.oracle_text:
Defender (This creature can't attack.)
{U}{U}, {T}: Create a 0/1 blue Plant Wall creature token with defender named Kelp.

research.note: Provides repeatable defensive bodies for convoke, sacrifice, or other broad token effects.
research.caution: Generated Kelp are Plant Walls with defender, not Saprolings; they cannot attack without a separate exception.
research.manaNote: Double blue to cast and another double blue for every activation makes it a poor splash.

cards.name: Weatherseed Totem
cards.oracle_text:
{T}: Add {G}.
{2}{G}{G}{G}: This artifact becomes a 5/3 green Treefolk artifact creature with trample until end of turn.
When this artifact is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, if it was a creature, return this card to its owner's hand.

research.note: A mana artifact later becomes a trampling Treefolk, supplying early utility and a threat in the same slot.
research.caution: It returns to hand on death only while it is a creature; repeated animation is expensive and does not remove summoning sickness.
research.manaNote: Costs three generic mana and taps for green; animation needs 2GGG.

cards.name: Wicker Warcrawler
cards.oracle_text: Whenever this creature attacks or blocks, put a -1/-1 counter on it at end of combat.

research.note: A wicker-themed artificial creature, useful as a lead if constructed botanical materials fit the box's scope.
research.caution: Its actual type is Scarecrow, not Plant or Golem. It acquires a -1/-1 counter at end of every combat in which it attacked or blocked, so its initially large body steadily deteriorates.

research.note: A wicker-themed Scarecrow with no rules text; a possible constructed-plant-material ally if that visual theme is accepted.
research.caution: It is a Scarecrow, not a Plant. Its inclusion is a material/theme proposal rather than a plant-subtype synergy, and it has no special botanical ability.

cards.name: Wickerbough Elder
cards.oracle_text:
This creature enters with a -1/-1 counter on it.
{G}, Remove a -1/-1 counter from this creature: Destroy target artifact or enchantment.

research.note: Provides interaction attached to an on-theme Treefolk and gets larger when its initial counter is removed.
research.caution: Cannot activate without a legal artifact or enchantment target and an available -1/-1 counter.
research.manaNote: Four mana with one green, then green for its interaction ability.

cards.name: Wizened Mentor
cards.oracle_text: Whenever an opponent activates an ability of a permanent that isn't a mana ability, you create a 1/1 white Zombie creature token. This ability triggers only once each turn.

research.note: A mummy cleric that produces Zombie tokens when opponents activate qualifying permanent abilities.
research.caution: Depends on the opposing packet containing relevant activated abilities; triggers only once each turn and excludes mana abilities.

cards.name: Wood Elemental
cards.oracle_text:
As this creature enters, sacrifice any number of untapped Forests.
Wood Elemental's power and toughness are each equal to the number of Forests sacrificed as it entered.

research.note: The owner's explicit example of a plant-themed creature whose actual type is Elemental. Keep it in the research pool regardless of its eventual power evaluation.
research.caution: It requires sacrificing untapped Forests as it enters; those lands cannot also be tapped to pay its spell cost. Sacrificing none leaves a 0/0, and a useful body costs substantial future mana production. It is not a Plant or Treefolk for subtype payoffs.
research.manaNote: Costs 3G, then needs additional untapped Forests to sacrifice; other basic land types cannot pay that entry requirement.

cards.name: Woodcaller Automaton
cards.oracle_text:
Prototype {2}{G}{G} — 3/3 (You may cast this spell with different mana cost, color, and size. It keeps its abilities and types.)
When this creature enters, if you cast it, untap target land you control. It becomes a Treefolk creature with haste and base power and toughness equal to this creature's power and toughness. It's still a land.

research.note: A wood-themed Construct that explicitly turns one of your lands into a Treefolk creature, connecting a non-Treefolk card to genuine Treefolk support.
research.caution: The Automaton is a Construct, not a Treefolk. The land-animation trigger requires that the Automaton was cast, so merely returning it from a graveyard does not trigger it. Animating a land exposes mana to creature removal.
research.manaNote: Costs 10 normally or 2GG as a prototype; the animated land's base size uses the Automaton's power and toughness.

cards.name: Woodvine Elemental
cards.oracle_text:
Trample
Parley — Whenever this creature attacks, each player reveals the top card of their library. For each nonland card revealed this way, attacking creatures you control get +1/+1 until end of turn. Then each player draws a card.

research.note: The owner's additional explicit botanical Elemental example. Its attack trigger can strengthen all your attacking creatures, regardless of their creature types, so it can support Plants, Treefolk, Fungi, or other allies.
research.caution: Parley reveals cards and then gives every player a draw, including opponents. The power boost depends on revealed nonlands and scales with player count. Woodvine itself is an Elemental, not a Plant or Treefolk.
research.manaNote: Costs 4GW, so it needs both green and white mana.

cards.name: Woodwraith Strangler
cards.oracle_text: Exile a creature card from your graveyard: Regenerate this creature.

research.note: A Plant Zombie that consumes a creature card from its controller's graveyard to regenerate.
research.caution: Regeneration is not returning a dead creature; exiling graveyard creatures competes with recursion and undergrowth.
research.manaNote: Requires black and green to cast; its activated ability has no mana cost.

cards.name: Wrap in Vigor
cards.oracle_text: Regenerate each creature you control.

research.note: A botanical regeneration effect can preserve a mixed board through combat or ordinary destruction.
research.caution: Regeneration differs from indestructible: it replaces a destruction event, taps the creature, and does not stop exile or sacrifice.
research.manaNote: Two mana with one green pip.

cards.name: Wrenn and Realmbreaker
cards.oracle_text:
Lands you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color."
+1: Up to one target land you control becomes a 3/3 Elemental creature with vigilance, hexproof, and haste until your next turn. It's still a land.
−2: Mill three cards. You may put a permanent card from among the milled cards into your hand.
−7: You get an emblem with "You may play lands and cast permanent spells from your graveyard."

research.note: A Treefolk-associated planeswalker that animates any land as an Elemental and lets all your lands provide any color, tying land creatures to multicolor support.
research.caution: Adds planeswalker rules, milling, and graveyard play. Its animation is temporary and does not untap the land. The emblem allows normal play/casting rather than free spells.
research.manaNote: Costs 1GG before it can help fix other colors.

cards.name: Wrenn and Seven
cards.oracle_text:
+1: Reveal the top four cards of your library. Put all land cards revealed this way into your hand and the rest into your graveyard.
0: Put any number of land cards from your hand onto the battlefield tapped.
−3: Create a green Treefolk creature token with reach and "This token's power and toughness are each equal to the number of lands you control."
−8: Return all permanent cards from your graveyard to your hand. You get an emblem with "You have no maximum hand size."

research.note: Creates a Treefolk scaled by lands, develops a landfall plan, and can fill the graveyard for later recovery.
research.caution: Five-mana planeswalker with several modes adds complexity; its zero ability needs lands in hand rather than searching for them.
research.manaNote: Five mana including double green; starting loyalty is five.

cards.name: Yavimaya Sapherd
cards.oracle_text: When this creature enters, create a 1/1 green Saproling creature token.

research.note: A straightforward Fungus plus Saproling offers two bodies for convoke, sacrifice, or creature-count effects.
research.caution: Its small bodies rely on the rest of the deck for a late-game plan.
research.manaNote: Three mana with one green pip.

research.note: Selected for v0.1 Restless Dead: Simple larger Zombie finisher..
research.caution: Provisional selection; evaluate in the combined forty-card pairings.

cards.name: Zombie Infestation
cards.oracle_text: Discard two cards: Create a 2/2 black Zombie creature token.

research.note: Turns spare cards into Zombies while placing useful creatures or flashback spells in the graveyard for later recovery.
research.caution: Each 2/2 costs two discarded cards; without sufficient card supply or graveyard value it empties the hand quickly.
research.manaNote: Costs 1B; its token-making ability has no mana cost but requires discarding two cards.
